findings.current: I knew. I had only been waiting.
findings.defect: The direct statement loses the emphatic double negation contrasting ignorance with deliberate waiting.
findings.rationale: 모르지 않았다 explicitly rejects the idea that he did not know; that pragmatic correction sets up his claim that he was knowingly waiting for the betrayal.
findings.replacement: It wasn’t that I didn’t know. I had only been waiting.

findings.current: Waiting for the moment they bared their fangs.
findings.defect: The draft changes thrusting or sinking their fangs into merely displaying them, weakening the anticipated act from an attack to a revelation of hostility.
findings.rationale: 송곳니를 들이밀다 describes putting the fangs into the target, matching the physical betrayal that immediately follows.
findings.replacement: Waiting for the moment they sank their fangs into me.

findings.current: A sound rang out behind me—the sound of three streaks of wind cutting into the vital points throughout my body.
findings.defect: The draft says the three attacks cut into his vital points, falsely implying that they struck him before the next sentence establishes that all three missed.
findings.rationale: 파고드는 describes the streaks bearing down on the targeted vital points, not successfully penetrating them.
findings.replacement: The sound of displaced air rang out behind me. Three streaks of wind bored toward vital points across my body.
findings.source: 등 뒤에서 파공성이 일었다. 전신 요혈을 파고드는 세 줄기의 바람.

findings.current: “You aren’t someone you can handle. Wait for a moment.”
findings.defect: The subject has been reversed into a nonsensical claim that Wu cannot handle himself; Lee is warning Wu that Jin is beyond him.
findings.rationale: 자네가 is the subject of 상대할 수 있는, while 자 refers to Jin Taekyung.
findings.replacement: “He’s not someone you can handle. Wait here for a moment.”
findings.source: “자네가 상대할 수 있는 자가 아니야. 잠시 기다리게.”

findings.current: “There’s no need for that. I only regret what happened.”
findings.defect: The first sentence no longer denies Jin’s accusation that Lee might blame his subordinates, and the second adds an unsupported object for Lee’s regret.
findings.rationale: 그럴 리가 rejects the proposed excuse, while 애석할 뿐이다 deliberately leaves what Lee regrets unstated until his next line.
findings.replacement: “Of course I wouldn’t. I merely find it regrettable.”

findings.current: “‘A good Chinese is a dead Chinese. Fucking Lee Jungryong.’ Those are the epitaphs I just came up with for you two. Do you like them?”
findings.defect: The draft sanitizes 짱깨, an explicit anti-Chinese slur, to the neutral word “Chinese,” weakening Jin’s deliberately vicious answer to Wu’s ethnic abuse.
findings.rationale: 착짱죽짱 compresses the slur 짱깨 into a hostile slogan; preserving its offensiveness is necessary to match the source’s profanity and register.
findings.replacement: “‘The only good chink is a dead chink. Fucking Lee Jungryong.’ Those are the epitaphs I just came up with for you two. Do you like them?”
findings.source: “착짱죽짱. 개씹정룡. 내가 방금 정한 너희 묘비명인데, 마음에 드냐?”

findings.current: The five hundred Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters who rose from death and charged gloriously.
findings.defect: “Rose from death” implies that the five hundred Hunters were resurrected, changing a scene fact in a fantasy setting where resurrection is materially distinct.
findings.rationale: 죽음을 딛고 일어나 means rising despite or in defiance of death, while 장렬히 describes their heroic, death-defying charge.
findings.replacement: The five hundred Public Security Armed Forces Department Hunters who rose in defiance of death and charged valiantly.
findings.source: 죽음을 딛고 일어나 장렬히 돌격하던 오백 명의 공안무력부 헌터들.

findings.current:
Wu Heixing curled his lips and spoke.

“Why should I take that kind of risk?”
findings.defect: The draft removes Wu’s repeated 왜, eliminating the distinctive verbal repetition that Jin fixates on and later throws back at him.
findings.rationale: 왜 내가 왜 deliberately repeats “why”; retaining it is necessary for the later quotation to function as an exact callback.
findings.replacement:
Wu Heixing curled his lips and spoke.

“Why—why should I take that kind of risk?”
findings.source: 「왜 내가 왜 그런 위험을 감수해야 하지?」

findings.current:
Then a sentence Lee Jungryong had heard somewhere before slipped from Jin Taekyung’s lips.

“Why should I take that kind of risk?”
findings.defect: The callback again removes the repeated “why,” so Jin no longer reproduces Wu’s conspicuous wording exactly.
findings.rationale: The source repeats Wu’s earlier line verbatim for the reversal; the English callback must retain the same verbal hitch.
findings.replacement:
Then a sentence Lee Jungryong had heard somewhere before slipped from Jin Taekyung’s lips.

“Why—why should I take that kind of risk?”
findings.source: “왜 내가 왜 그런 위험을 감수해야 하지?”

findings.current: It was a strike Lee Jungryong had unleashed with complete sincerity, one he had not shown anywhere else in this war.
findings.defect: “Complete sincerity” is an unnatural literalism that obscures the mechanical point that Lee is attacking in earnest with his full power.
findings.rationale: 진심을 담아 in this combat context means Lee has become serious and is putting his full strength into the blow, not that the strike is emotionally sincere.
findings.replacement: It was a full-power strike from Lee Jungryong, the likes of which he had not unleashed anywhere else in this war.
findings.source: 이번 전쟁 어디에서도 보인 적 없던, 이정룡이 진심을 담아 휘두른 일격이다.

findings.current: Superheated air burned as it surged upward.
findings.defect: The draft changes the subject from blazing heat that burns the air to the air itself surging upward.
findings.rationale: 열기가 is the subject that 타올랐다, while 공기를 is the object of 태우며.
findings.replacement: Superheated flames blazed up, burning the air.

summary: The draft contains one reversed subject, one false implication that an attack connected, a resurrection-like mistrendering, and several meaningful losses of negation, repetition, force, and profanity.
